chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who is left-handed or right-handed who stole, he said: His right hand is cut off in all cases.

key_terms.أَشَلَّ: A person who is missing a hand or has a disability in one hand
key_terms.عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ: In all cases / regardless of the situation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on amputating the hand of a thief who is disabled in one hand?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the standard limb for hadd amputation is the right hand, irrespective of the thief's natural handedness or existing disability in the left hand. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the 'right hand' refers to the specific anatomical limb designated for the punishment, ensuring consistency in the application of justice regardless of individual physical variations.
